sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Principle of Partition**: The plan accepted the **Muslim League's demand** for Pakistan while ensuring the **territorial integrity** of India was maintained as much as possible.
• **Dominion Status**: Both India and Pakistan were to be granted **Dominion Status** with the right to secede from the British Commonwealth.
• **Principle of Self-Determination**: Provinces like **Punjab and Bengal** were given the right to vote for partition through their legislative assemblies.
• **Key Metric**: The date of transfer of power was advanced to **August 15, 1947**, to prevent further communal escalation.

The legislative enactment of the Mountbatten Plan by the British Parliament, which formally ended British rule and created the two dominions.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Princely States**: They were given the option to join either India or Pakistan or remain independent, effectively ending British Paramountcy.
• **Transfer of Power**: The process was expedited to avoid a power vacuum and civil war.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Massive communal violence, refugee crisis, and the integration of 565 Princely States.
• **Solutions**: Formation of the States Department under Sardar Patel and the use of Instrument of Accession.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-A-R-T' (Partition, Accession, Referendum, Transfer).
• **Decoded Meaning**: P-Partition of provinces, A-Accession of Princely States, R-Referendum in NWFP/Sylhet, T-Transfer of power by August 15.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Mountbatten Plan' with the 'Cabinet Mission Plan'. Remember: Cabinet Mission (1946) rejected Pakistan; Mountbatten Plan (1947) accepted it.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Balkanization' to describe the threat posed by the Princely States' option to remain independent, which was averted by the diplomatic efforts of Sardar Patel.

keyTakeaways: The Mountbatten Plan was the final British attempt to exit India while managing communal tensions.
It introduced the concept of Dominion Status as a transitional phase.
The plan directly led to the Indian Independence Act, 1947, which legally partitioned the subcontinent.
